mutants.label: blackout-uses-utc-not-phoenix
mutants.why: Dropping .astimezone(PHOENIX) leaves start_local/end_local as the same absolute instants, only re-labeled tzinfo=UTC instead of America/Phoenix. Python compares aware datetimes by absolute instant regardless of the tzinfo label, so every `start_local <= local_window_end` / `local_window_start <= end_local` comparison is unaffected -- the local_window_* values are still built via datetime.combine(day, ..., tzinfo=PHOENIX), so they are correctly anchored. The only thing the missing astimezone changes is which calendar `day` the loop starts/ends on (`.date()` read off a UTC-labeled instant instead of a Phoenix one): PHOENIX is a fixed UTC-7 offset (no DST), so that shifts the UTC-derived date to the Phoenix date, or one day ahead, exactly when the Phoenix local hour is >=17 (i.e. once the day's own 05:45-07:15 window has already elapsed) -- so a 'skipped' day can never be a day whose window a forward-looking interval could still reach. Verified empirically, not just argued: a brute-force comparison of the real and mutated implementations across 2,040,000 (now_utc, horizon_s) pairs -- 2,000,000 random draws over a 10-year span with horizons from 0s to 2 days, plus an exhaustive minute-by-minute sweep of 5 calendar days at horizons {0, 60, 900, 3600, 86400, 90000}s -- found zero mismatches.
